options.A: Is entirely non-conscious matter and processes
options.B: Has no consciousness but deserves ethical consideration
options.C: Has something analogous to but different from consciousness
options.D: Has some form of awareness or proto-sentience

items.text: Indigenous cultures treating nature as alive and aware is:

options.D: May capture something real we've lost sight of
options.E: Closer to literal truth than modern materialism

items.text: Does a forest "want" anything? Does the earth have interests?

options.A: No—only conscious beings have wants and interests
options.B: No, but we can speak metaphorically about ecological needs
options.D: Probably—complex systems can have something like interests
options.E: Yes—nature has its own aims and interests

interpretation.-1: Nature has no consciousness but ethical standing
interpretation.1: Nature has some form of awareness
